records.name: Bolu
records.current_summary:
Every province in Türkiye sits under the same intensifying national framework. A leaked draft of the 11th Judicial Package (October 2025) would criminalise LGBT conduct and advocacy — up to 3 years for behaviour 'contrary to biological sex and general morality' and 4 years for same-sex ceremonies — and would raise gender-affirming-care eligibility from 18 to 25 with a permanent-infertility mandate, exposing providers to fines and up to 7 years and patients to up to 3 years; 15 LGBT groups and the Turkish Medical Association objected. The Kaos GL 2025 human-rights report ('A Major Siege', published February 2026) finds hostility became explicit state policy in 2025 — presidency-centred, implemented through the family ministry — documenting 6 right-to-life violations including 3 hate-motivated killings with trans people most affected, 89 torture or ill-treatment cases (up from 51) and 313 liberty violations (about 2.5-fold), counted from media coverage because the state keeps no hate-crime statistics.

No province-specific ordinance, incident series or court decision concerning trans visitors in Bolu was documented in this research pass; the national framework above is the whole documented picture for Bolu. The absence of recorded provincial enforcement is not evidence of local tolerance, and equally not evidence of a local ban.

sources.claim: Human Rights Watch news release (29 Oct 2025) on the leaked '11th Judicial Package' draft omnibus law: would amend the Turkish penal and civil codes to criminalise behaviour deemed 'contrary to biological sex and general morality', criminalise taking part in a same-sex engagement or marriage ceremony (penalties up to 4 years in prison), raise the minimum age for gender-affirming health care including surgery from 18 to 25 with mandatory permanent infertility, and punish health professionals who perform such care - HRW calls it one of the most alarming rollbacks of LGBT rights in decades, and 15 Turkish LGBT groups plus the Turkish Medical Association oppose the draft.

Kaos GL report launch on the 2025 report 'A major siege against LGBTI+ people in 2025: Hostility turned into state policy': documents that anti-LGBTI+ hostility became institutionalised as explicit state policy, with senior officials' hate speech and instructions issued to public institutions under a 'Year of the Family' banner creating a climate that encouraged human-rights violations, and regulatory/supervisory bodies systematically restricting freedom of expression and artistic freedom; findings were presented by lawyer Kerem Dikmen at the launch.

records.name: Kahramanmaraş
records.current_summary: No province-specific trans-related signal found in this research pass: the national framework and its 2025-26 escalation apply here unchanged. The region's sources are national-level: a leaked draft omnibus reform package (11th Judicial Package, October 2025) would create new anti-LGBT articles — criminalising conduct deemed "contrary to biological sex and general morality", restricting gender-affirming healthcare with a minimum age of 25, and enabling charges against trans people and their providers; and the state's "Year of the Family" institutional programme and blanket bans on LGBTI public events are national practice, not provincial choices. The absence of a documented provincial ban is not evidence of tolerance — the national blanket-ban practice applies across the country.

sources.claim: HRW (29 Oct 2025) reports a leaked draft of Türkiye's omnibus '11th Judicial Package' that would amend the penal code to imprison for up to 3 years people who incite or 'promote' conduct deemed contrary to biological sex and general morality, criminalise participation in same-sex engagement or marriage ceremonies with penalties up to 4 years, and restrict gender-affirming health care to people 25 and over under mandatory permanent infertility, exposing providers to fines and up to 7 years and patients to up to 3 years in prison; 15 LGBT groups and the Turkish Medical Association objected. No Kahramanmaraş-specific statute, incident or court case appears in the document; it supports this record's claim that the national framework applies to the province.

Kaos GL's report on 2025 ('A Major Siege against LGBTI+ People in 2025: Hostility Turned into State Policy') documents six right-to-life violations, three recorded as hate-motivated killings with trans people most affected, counted from media and civil-society reports because the state keeps no hate-crime statistics; 89 torture or ill-treatment violations (up from 51), mostly linked to peaceful assembly; and 313 liberty violations, about 2.5 times the previous year, mostly detentions. It reports hostility institutionalised under 'Year of the Family' instructions to public institutions, hate speech from senior officials, and artistic events cancelled or banned, presented as national practice rather than provincial choice. No Kahramanmaraş-specific finding appears; the source supports this record's claims about the country-wide framework.
